title: Opponent-pool resume identity provenance repair
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: Restoring next_id from both active snapshots and candidate history prevents rejected candidate IDs from being reused across exact-state continuation without changing pool weights or active membership.
material_change: Update OpponentPool.load_from_checkpoint to advance next_id past every serialized candidate-history ID and add focused regression coverage for pruned candidates, malformed metadata, and subsequent add identity.
baseline: Current loader derives next_id only from retained active snapshots; seed2/3 of the completed static current-KL 262k experiment reused previously rejected IDs while full tuple refs remained causally unambiguous.
notes: Focused dynamic-pool suite passed 8/8 after adding rejected-ID and malformed-history regression cases. The repair changes only resume-time identity allocation; frozen checkpoints and existing raw evaluation evidence are unchanged.

result.summary: OpponentPool resume now advances next_id beyond both active snapshot IDs and every valid serialized candidate-history ID. Two new regressions reproduce the pruned-candidate reuse condition and malformed-history compatibility; the broader dynamic-pool, ELO-pool, and replay suites pass 23/23.
result.conclusion: The seed2/3 candidate-ID reuse observed in the completed 262k experiment was a real provenance defect but noncausal there because reused predecessors were rejected, active IDs stayed unique, and assignment refs included unique iteration/hands tuples. Future resumes will retain monotonic candidate identity.
result.next_step: Run an independent higher-precision fresh-only matched confirmation on the already frozen 65k and 262k endpoints; use its predeclared breadth and replication gates to decide whether static current-KL merits 1M-scale training.
